notes:
Summary: Mid-market SaaS (Brightline) building AI-driven support + search features. Completed a 2-week Hosted API POC; now evaluating Dedicated for predictable throughput and cost controls. Team wants committed capacity to hit latency SLOs and lower per-token cost.

POC technical takeaways:
- Integration: used Node SDK + backend proxy. No data plane issues.
- Traffic profile (observed during 14-day run): baseline QPS ~12, steady-state QPS ~25, weekday peak QPS spikes to ~110-130 (evenings PST), concurrency peaks ~120 concurrent requests during peak hour.
- Token mix: 60% short queries (<64 tokens), 30% medium (64-512 tokens), 10% long/responses (>=1024 tokens). Avg input tokens ~45, avg output tokens ~220.
- Daily token volume: current prodish estimate ~1.8-2.2M tokens/day; target scale for launch is 3-5M tokens/day in Q3.
- Latency: Hosted 95th tail ~300-450ms for medium prompts; goal with Dedicated ~120-180ms 95th.
- Error profile: transient 503s under burst; SE suspects autoscaling cold start / queueing.

Requirements / asks:
- Dedicated sizing: want recommendation for GPU pools (gauge for 8k vs 32k context model variants), expected qps concurrency headroom, and burst capacity.
- Routing: model routing by latency vs cost; fallback to smaller model during overload.
- Security: must have SOC2, SSO (SAML), audit logs, EU data residency for EU customers.
- Pricing: price sensitivity around committed discount; acceptable blended cost target <$0.004/1k tokens (aiming for 20-30% discount with commit).

Commercial notes:
- Budget: evaluating with PM and finance; rough procurement window Apr 2026. ARR target for Redwood: $150k-$300k ARR committed first year.
- Decision influencers: Head of Platform (technical), VP Product (cost/UX), Legal (DPA/residency).

Next steps:
1) SE to deliver capacity-sizing workbook with modeled QPS/concurrency and recommended pool sizes (ETA 2026-03-17).
2) Pricing slide with committed tiers + burst pricing (follow-up call 2026-03-19).
3) Legal to start DPA review (we provided security deck; Brightline to return questions).
